headline: Constitutional Council approves France's assisted-dying law
description: The legislation grants adults suffering from an incurable condition the right to assisted dying. The Council's decision is a victory for President Emmanuel Macron, who promised such a law when he was re-elected for a second term in 2022.

French taxpayers' data stolen in hack of Finance Ministry
description: The Finance Ministry acknowledged on Thursday that it had fallen victim to another cyberattack. The full extent of the breach remained unclear, but it could concern several hundred thousand people in France.

headline: Japan's pacifist identity is shaken by a world where military might prevails
description: Article 9 of the Constitution, which states that Japan 'renounces war forever,' is being challenged by regional instability and doubts over the enduring reliability of American support.

headline: British far right's leader Farage beats Count Binface to win by-election
description: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage won with 63% of the vote in an election that was boycotted by the major parties. A parliamentary probe into undisclosed gifts he received was subsequently reopened.

headline: One-person households' struggle for housing: 'It would be much easier as a couple. I feel like I'm being punished twice'
description: Some 12 million people live alone in France, and their number continues to rise. The country's housing stock has not kept pace with this trend, exacerbating the impact of the housing crisis on these individuals.

description: 'My Breasts and Me' (5/5). In France, one out of every two patients chooses the private sector for breast reconstruction. Some are willing to give up their vacations, take out a loan or turn to their parents for help. Le Monde spent several weeks inside a private breast surgery practice in Paris.

headline: 'It was either exile or prison': An interview with Boris Nadezhdin, Putin opponent who fled to France
description: The veteran Russian politician, 63, tried to challenge Vladimir Putin's regime and its war in Ukraine through legal and electoral means. He failed. Facing the threat of arrest, he decided to leave Russia. His interview with Le Monde is his first since arriving in France.

headline: Finland wants to restore its peatlands to help the environment. And to slow Russian tanks.
description: The Nordic country has identified 180,000 hectares of wetlands that, if restored, could benefit not only the climate and biodiversity but also national defense. While the military supports the plan, some environmentalists warn against rushing the process.
